title: Zdravo, Sarajevo!
reviewerNotes: Exemplar chapter. ready for human review before publish.
storyBeat: Ana lands in Sarajevo and takes her first walk through Baščaršija, practicing greetings and new letter sounds.

vocabulary: Basic greetings (zdravo, dobar dan, hvala, molim)
The full Latin Bosnian alphabet, including č ć š ž đ dž lj nj
grammar: All 30 Latin Bosnian letters (A to Ž), with sound examples
How to type accented letters on a plain keyboard
Simple greeting exchanges (no full conjugation yet)
culture: Baščaršija as Sarajevo’s old bazaar heart
Warm everyday greetings in Bosnia and Herzegovina

grammar.title: The full Latin Bosnian alphabet
grammar.explanation: Bosnian in this course uses the Latin script only (no Cyrillic). There are 30 letters. Most match English. Learn the whole row first, then zoom in on the special ones. Order: A B C Č Ć D Dž Đ E F G H I J K L Lj M N Nj O P R S Š T U V Z Ž. Digraphs Dž, Lj, and Nj count as single letters in the alphabet.

grammar.title: Writing č ć š ž đ
grammar.explanation: Bosnian uses letters that many English keyboards do not show by default: č ć š ž đ (and capitals Č Ć Š Ž Đ). You must write them correctly in real Bosnian. On a phone, long-press c, s, z, or d to find the letter. On a computer, use a Bosnian keyboard layout or insert the character from your system tools. In this course, practice answers expect the real letters.

grammar.title: Greeting exchanges
grammar.explanation: Start simple. Say a greeting, hear one back, then add hvala or molim. Formal day greetings use dobar dan; friends often say zdravo.

culture.title: Baščaršija, Sarajevo’s old heart
culture.body: Baščaršija is the historic bazaar of Sarajevo: narrow streets, copper shops, cafés, and the sound of footsteps on stone. Ana arrives with a backpack and a phrase list. Shopkeepers greet visitors with a warm Dobar dan! Learning greetings here is not just polite. It opens doors (and often a free smile). The special letters in Baščaršija (š, č) are your first real Bosnian workout.

lessonBlocks.title: Lesson A: Walk the full alphabet
lessonBlocks.body: Say the whole Latin Bosnian alphabet out loud once: A B C Č Ć D Dž Đ E F G H I J K L Lj M N Nj O P R S Š T U V Z Ž. That is thirty letters. Digraphs Dž, Lj, and Nj are single alphabet letters even though they look like two characters. Now zoom in on the ones English does not have: Č č (church), Ć ć (softer/shorter), Dž dž (jam), Đ đ (softer j), Š š (ship), Ž ž (measure), plus Lj lj and Nj nj. Practice words: čaj, ćup, džezva, đak, šuma, žena, ljubav (love), njega (care). Ana drills them on the plane, then spots Baščaršija on a sign and finally hears the letters in a real street name.
tips: Do not skip the boring letters. C (ts) is not English C, and J is like English Y.
č vs ć: č is harder; ć is softer and shorter
Write č ć š ž đ correctly. Do not replace them with plain c s z d.

lessonBlocks.title: Lesson B: Your first greetings
lessonBlocks.body: Memorize this mini set: Zdravo (hi), Dobar dan (good day), Dobro jutro (good morning), Dobra večer (good evening), Hvala (thanks), Molim (please / you're welcome), Doviđenja (goodbye), Da / Ne (yes / no). Use Dobar dan with people you do not know well. Use Zdravo with friends, or with Emir once you meet him tomorrow. Notice doviđenja needs đ; večer needs č. Write the special letters carefully when you practice.
tips: Smile helps more than perfect pronunciation
If you forget, Hvala still works almost everywhere

funFacts.title: Baščaršija means ‘main market’
funFacts.body: The name comes from Turkish roots meaning the chief marketplace. Today it is still full of craft shops and cafés.

funFacts.title: One letter, one sound
funFacts.body: Bosnian spelling is mostly phonetic: what you see is what you say. That helps beginners a lot once the special letters click.

funFacts.title: Cats of the čaršija
funFacts.body: Sarajevo’s old town is famous for friendly street cats. Mrvica is fictional, but her attitude is very local.

questions.question: What does 'zdravo' mean?
questions.explanation: Zdravo is the friendly everyday hello.

questions.question: Which greeting is more polite with strangers during the day?
questions.explanation: Dobar dan is the polite daytime greeting.

questions.question: Which word means 'thank you'?
questions.explanation: Hvala = thank you. Molim can mean please or you're welcome.

questions.question: How many letters are in the Latin Bosnian alphabet?
questions.explanation: Latin Bosnian has 30 letters. Dž, Lj, and Nj each count as one letter.

questions.question: The letter š sounds most like English…
questions.explanation: Š is like sh in ship. as in Baščaršija.

questions.question: A džezva is…
questions.explanation: Džezva is the little pot used for Bosnian coffee.

questions.question: How do you say goodbye?
questions.explanation: Doviđenja means goodbye. The letter đ Needs the letter đ.

questions.question: Baščaršija is…
questions.explanation: Baščaršija is the historic market heart of Sarajevo.

questions.question: Which pair shows a harder vs softer 'ch'-like sound?
options: dž vs đ only as vowels
questions.explanation: Č is harder; ć is softer. a classic beginner pair.

civicContext.title: International oversight still sits above elected offices
civicContext.body: After the 1995 Dayton Peace Agreement, the Office of the High Representative was created to oversee civilian implementation of the peace deal. Under the Bonn Powers, the High Representative can impose laws and remove public officials, which means an internationally appointed office can overrule decisions made inside Bosnia and Herzegovina’s elected institutions. That arrangement is a documented limit on ordinary sovereignty: final say does not always rest with local voters.
